description: Sets, removes or lists breakpoints. A set on a script that is not there, or past its last line, is refused, as nothing would ever stop there; a remove takes any line, and with no editor connected answers removed false, saying why, when none was held there. Set them first, then editor_run, and the game stops where you asked. With the editor connected it goes through the editor's debug adapter; with none, it is held here. A game this server starts itself, which editor_run start does for a run given args, savesIn, env or silent, or with no editor, is handed every breakpoint held here as it starts, and one set while that game runs reaches it at once (runningGame says so). The editor keeps a breakpoint set this way for one play, so every breakpoint this server holds is sent again before each play editor_run starts, and the start answer lists them under breakpoints. The set is also kept in the project, for the server that comes after a reconnect: a breakpoint stays until it is removed here, whichever server set it. Every answer lists the whole set under held, and the breakpoints the user set in the editor's own gutter under setInEditor; setting one here never takes those away, and removing a line here clears it whoever set it. Godot clears every breakpoint in the editor when a debug session opens unless network/debug_adapter/sync_breakpoints is on, which the addon turns on as it loads; an editor where it was turned off again is said so under breakpointsAtRisk, here and in editor_status. Operations: set (needs scriptPath, line): set a breakpoint; remove (needs scriptPath, line): remove a breakpoint; list: the breakpoints held here under held, and with the editor connected the ones set in its gutter under setInEditor.

line.description: One-based line. Only for ops set, remove.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

scriptPath.description: Script file inside the project, such as "scripts/player.gd". Only for ops set, remove.
